Add Assistant grabber accessibility ID and Medium detent EG test

EarlGrey swipe actions always run to the window edge, so EG tests can't
reliably stop the Assistant sheet at the Medium detent: swipes from
Minimized always land on Large, and fast swipes from Large land on
Minimized. No EG test enters Medium from another detent today.

Tapping the grabber is deterministic: each tap moves the sheet to the
next taller detent, and from Large back to Minimized. This CL:
- Gives the grabber button an accessibility identifier, so tests can
  match it without relying on its localized label. There is no
  user-visible change.
- Adds a `TapGrabberAndWaitForDetent()` helper to the AIM EG tests.
- Adds `testGrabberCyclesDetents`, which goes Medium -> Large ->
  Minimized -> Medium with grabber taps.

Deflake WPT COOP iframe-popup-same-origin-to-* tests

In resources/iframe-test.js:

1. Run subtests sequentially with promise_test instead of
promise_test_parallel, and clean up each subtest's iframe and popup
via t.add_cleanup (waiting for the popup to acknowledge before
closing) instead of add_completion_callback. Previously, all 6
subtests in a variant ran concurrently and kept all 6 iframes and 6
popups alive polling /common/dispatcher/dispatcher.py until the entire
test file completed, saturating the 6-socket-per-origin HTTP/1.1 pool.
2. In the 'severed' opener state with window_open, poll popup.closed in
the iframe up to 2.5s instead of relying on a fixed 500ms timer that
could race cross-process WindowProxy detachment IPC under load.
3. Remove the obsolete unparameterized [ Skip Timeout ] entries for
iframe-popup-same-origin-to-unsafe-none.https.html and
iframe-popup-same-origin-to-same-origin.https.html, as well as the
Linux [ Failure Pass ] entry for
iframe-popup-same-origin-to-unsafe-none.https.html?*, from
TestExpectations.

Don't tick static animations that can't be composited

An animation whose values can't change while it's in play, such as the
view transition `mix-blend-mode: plus-lighter` animation, can only
change at a phase boundary, so it doesn't need main thread ticks.
Animation::PreCommit() already skips ticking such animations, but only
if having no visible change is the only reason for not compositing
them. Any other reason, e.g. affecting an !important property, made
them tick on the main thread every frame for their whole duration.

For example, `::view-transition-old(*), ::view-transition-new(*) {
mix-blend-mode: normal !important }`, which opts out of the
plus-lighter blending, made the plus-lighter animations of every view
transition group tick on the main thread, even though their values are
overridden and can't change.

This patch skips ticking an animation if all of its properties are
static, regardless of other reasons for not compositing it, behind the
SkipTickingStaticAnimations kill switch. The full compositing
disposition is still reported for tracing and UMA.

Improve FilePersistentMemoryAllocator Windows flushing

On Windows, ::FlushViewOfFile() writes modified pages only to the
operating system cache, not to the underlying physical disk. When a
synchronous flush is requested, calling ::FlushFileBuffers() on the
underlying file handle after flushing the mapped view ensures data
is durably committed to physical media and survives sudden system
termination or power loss.

Because ::FlushFileBuffers() can introduce significant disk I/O
latency, gate this behind a new base::features feature
(kFlushFileBuffersOnSyncFlush, disabled by default) per reviewer
recommendation to allow evaluating its performance cost/benefit.

In production, the sole synchronous flush call path is triggered by
MetricsService::RecordCurrentEnvironment() in components/metrics:
  allocator->memory_allocator()->Flush(/*sync=*/true);
This call is gated behind the kFlushPersistentSystemProfileOnWrite
feature experiment and dispatched asynchronously to a background
ThreadPool task runner with TaskPriority::BEST_EFFORT and MayBlock().
When kFlushFileBuffersOnSyncFlush is enabled, calling
::FlushFileBuffers() ensures the updated system profile is safely
committed to physical storage, protecting against unparsable
corrupted profiles across sudden power loss or OS crashes, while
avoiding any UI thread blocking.

[wpt] Fix guaranteed timeout in COOP access-reporting/reporting-observer

The last subtest ("Access from cross-site iframe") expects *no*
coop-access-violation report and calls `receive(this_window_token, 2000)`
expecting it to resolve with "timeout". However, dispatcher.js's
`receive()` only takes a uuid and polls the dispatcher forever; the 2000
is silently ignored. Because Chromium correctly never dispatches a report
here, the subtest can never complete and the whole test always hits the
harness timeout (150s in Debug) and gets its content_shell killed.

Use the directory's existing `receiveReport()` helper from
reporting-common.js instead, which races the dispatcher against a 3s
step_timeout and returns "timeout" when nothing arrives, so the subtest
completes in a few seconds. The test now passes deterministically on
Linux, so drop the [ Pass Timeout ] expectation.

[Extensions] Make SW registration state explicit

ServiceWorkerTaskQueue tracks the activations whose worker is registered
in a set, worker_registered_. When an activation isn't in the set,
there's no way to tell whether its registration is in progress or
failed. Follow-up fixes for the linked bug need that distinction, and
another parallel set would make the registration logic even harder to
follow.

Replace the set with a RegistrationState (kNotRegistered, kRegistering
or kRegistered) in ServiceWorkerState, which already holds the rest of
the worker state of an activation. As before, only registered workers
are started. This also resolves a TODO to move the registration check
into ServiceWorkerState.

AddPendingTask() now looks up the worker state for every task. If it's
missing, which isn't expected, the task is still queued as before, but a
CHECK that isn't fatal until M160 reports it.

No behavior change. In particular, the worker stays kRegistered during a
re-registration after a verification mismatch, even if it fails. A
follow-up fixes this.

[GEiC] Add GlicProviderSpec owned by GlicKeyedService

Adds GlicProviderSpec, a stateless per-provider interface that Glic code
reads provider-specific values from (consumer Gemini vs Gemini
Enterprise) instead of branching on GlicProvider. It has value members
only and no identity accessor.

GlicKeyedService creates the concrete spec once per profile by checking
geic::IsGeicEnabled() and exposes it via provider_spec(). The settings
AI section, OpenGlicSettingsPage's subpage and the GlicButton entry-point
icon now read their values from the spec, which removes those
GlicEnabling::GetProviderForProfile() callers.

[Omnibox] Deflake OmniboxActionsTest#testActionInSuggestShown

Previously, resolveKeyboardTransition() prematurely set mKeyboardState
to SHOWN or HIDDEN as soon as the debounce timer fired (0ms in tests)
instead of keeping mKeyboardState in SHOWING or HIDING until the OS
confirmed the visibility change via keyboardVisibilityChanged(). This
left mKeyboardState out of sync with asynchronous IME transitions and
required ad-hoc workarounds in setKeyboardVisibilityDebounced(). In
addition, OmniboxActionsTest#tearDown() skipped mOmniboxUtils.clearFocus()
after action chip clicks because clickOnAction() cleared UrlBar focus
synchronously while the toolbar unfocus animation and soft keyboard
dismissal were still in flight.

Fix this by:
1. Keeping mKeyboardState in SHOWING/HIDING in
   resolveKeyboardTransition() until the OS notifies
   keyboardVisibilityChanged().
2. Only fast-cancelling a transiting state in
   setKeyboardVisibilityDebounced() if mKeyboardTransitionRunnable is
   still pending on the handler, and re-posting the hide runnable if a
   late OS show callback arrives while HIDING.
3. Waiting for toolbar focus animations to complete at the end of
   OmniboxTestUtils#requestFocus() and unconditionally calling
   mOmniboxUtils.clearFocus() in OmniboxActionsTest#tearDown().

[WebUI Toolbar] Fix null deref in WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::AimButtonVisible

WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::AimButtonVisible() dereferenced the result of
AiModePageActionController::From() without checking it for null.

During browser shutdown,
BrowserWindowFeatures::TearDownPreBrowserWindowDestruction() destroys
the AiModePageActionController before the BrowserWidget is destroyed.
~Widget then clears focus, which blurs the WebUI toolbar web view and
calls WebUIReadOnlyOmnibox::OnBlur(). That leads to RequestUpdateWebUI()
-> ComputeMojoState() -> AimButtonVisible(), where From() now returns
nullptr, and the browser crashes.

40bccac8bec8e972763c934af671278b21cadb36 [ diff ] 
Android: Use FromReflectedMethod in InputHintChecker

InputHintChecker::HasInputImpl() is polled every 1ms on the Browser UI
thread (kYieldWithInputHint), previously invoking
android.view.View#probablyHasInput() via reflective Method.invoke() and
unboxing the boxed Boolean with Boolean.booleanValue().

Key changes and performance evidence:
* Resolve the direct jmethodID once during off-thread initialization via
  env->FromReflectedMethod() and invoke env->CallBooleanMethod()
  directly in HasInputImpl().
* Drops the reflect_method_for_has_input_ JNI global ref and shrinks
  sizeof(InputHintChecker) by 16 bytes.
* In a release build benchmark on Android 16 (x86_64, 1M calls across 10
  trials), this reduces HasInputImpl() mean wall time from 957.0 ns to
  259.0 ns (3.69x faster, 4.05x at p95) and thread CPU time from 940.1
  ns to 254.8 ns (-72.9%).
* Adds InputHintCheckerTest.RealViewInitialization in base_unittests.

[masonry] Test per-segment rule visibility

The CSSWG resolved that rule visibility applies per segment in grid
lanes. Our current implementation uses whole-lane occupancy, which can
leave rules visible beside empty portions of a lane.

Most of the coverage we had was with `rule-break: none`, which is not
affected by the resolution. So this CL adds coverage for `rule-break:
intersection`, and converts a test we had for `none` to be for
`intersection`. These are marked as failing, the implementation CL will
follow.

https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/14489.

[iOS][TTC] Extract TTCAudioSessionController from TTCAudioEngine

Split TTCAudioEngine into two focused classes:
- TTCAudioEngine (<TTCAudioEngineProtocol>): manages the AVAudioEngine
  graph, TTCAudioRecorder tap, and TTCAudioPlayer playback node.
- TTCAudioSessionController (<TTCAudioController>): owns
  TTCAudioSessionManager, microphone permissions, loopback, test-tone
  generation, and route change delegation over an injected or default
  id<TTCAudioEngineProtocol>.

Update TtcConversation default initializer to instantiate
TTCAudioSessionController and split the existing unit tests between
ttc_audio_engine_unittest.mm and ttc_audio_session_controller_unittest.mm.

Do not paint focus ring for display-locked <area> elements

When painting an <img> with an associated focused <area> element,
ImagePainter::PaintAreaElementFocusRing calls EnsureComputedStyle() on
the <area> to check for outlines.

In the linked bug, Blink attempts to paint a display-locked <area>
element. This triggers a style update mid-paint which leads to a
use-after-free.

This CL skips painting the focus ring if the <area> is display-locked.

Improve state sync for keyword mode to prevent click/switch mode exits

Previously, clicking a keyword chip and then clicking out of the
omnibox popup would exit keyword mode; but pressing Tab to enter
keyword mode would preserve the mode when clicking out that way.
Also previously, entering keyword mode on one tab, then switching to
another and back would incorrectly leave keyword mode exited.

Both issues were due to inconsistent state between webui and C++ which
this change resolves.

[Actor]: Register EnterFullscreenToolRequest in ToolRegistry

ToolRegistry provides a central catalog of browser tool schemas for
ActorKeyedService (go/actor-tool-registry-design). ToolRequest
subclasses expose their schema via static GetToolDefinition(), and
ToolRegistry discovers them at compile time through ToolRequestVariant.

Currently, EnterFullscreenToolRequest exists and is hooked up to the
Actor execution layer, but lacks a GetToolDefinition() implementation
and model-facing schema. As a result, ToolRegistry does not expose the
enter_fullscreen tool. TTC still dispatches fullscreen through its own
combined set_fullscreen tool with a boolean argument.

This CL registers EnterFullscreenToolRequest in ToolRegistry by adding
ToolId::kEnterFullscreen, declaring kModelFacingName
("enter_fullscreen"), and implementing GetToolDefinition() using
ToolDefinitionBuilder with no parameters. It also adds unit test
coverage in tool_registry_unittest.cc under desktop build guards, since
window_management_tool_request.h is excluded from Android builds. Its
partner exit_fullscreen is registered separately in crrev.com/c/8526144.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for ModalDialogWrapper

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

[updater] Add `app.icns to` the prod-signed updater test data.

crrev.com/c/8224743 started including the app icon in updater.zip, so
signed GoogleUpdater.app builds from branch 8067 onward carry
Contents/Resources/app.icns as a sealed resource. The roll of
chrome_mac_universal_prod to 156.0.8067.0 (crrev.com/c/8490954) picked
this up, but the test data list names the bundle's files one by one and
did not include the icon.

The bundle that reaches the test bots is therefore missing a sealed
resource and fails code signature validation. This breaks
`PrivilegedHelperTest.VerifyUpdaterSignature` and
`IntegrationTest.PrivilegedHelperInstall`.

Media Session: Track picture-in-picture state per player

Previously, `MediaSessionController::IsMediaSessionNeeded()` checked
`WebContentsImpl::HasPictureInPictureVideo()`, and
`MediaSessionControllersManager::PictureInPictureStateChanged()`
notified all controllers in the `WebContents` when Picture-in-Picture
state changed. As a result, any muted (`has_audio = false`) media player
in the `WebContents` would be added to `MediaSessionImpl` whenever
another player in the tab was in Picture-in-Picture.

This change tracks `is_in_picture_in_picture_` per
`MediaSessionController` and plumbs the `MediaPlayerId` from
`PictureInPictureSession` through
`VideoPictureInPictureWindowControllerImpl` and
`MediaWebContentsObserver` to `MediaSessionControllersManager`, so only
the player actually in Picture-in-Picture is added to the media session
on that basis.

When submitting a Composebox query with image context (such as a
screenshot or uploaded image) in Omnibox Everywhere, fulfill the query
via OpenUrlWithInPlaceWindow() in a new 800x600 browser window
horizontally center-aligned and vertically top-aligned with the popup

feature flag (enabled by default) and exposed in chrome://flags.

[InfoBar] Fix use-after-dtor in BrowserInfoBarManager::OnInfoBarRemoved

When a tab holding a global infobar instance is destroyed while its
renderer is still alive, the instance is removed in ~InfoBarManager().
By then the owning ContentInfoBarManager's WebContentsObserver base is
already destroyed, so WebContentsFromInfoBar() reads a destroyed object.
With MigratedAutomation on, this broke Linux MSan Tests and caused the
revert of crrev.com/c/8399828
(https://ci.chromium.org/b/8668754445962996305).

Thus, this CL changes to read the WebContents from the delegate instead.
There is no behavior change: on teardown its web_contents() is already
null, so OnInfoBarRemoved() still returns early.

Also adds GlobalInstanceRemovedDuringTabDestruction, a regression
browser test.

[a11y] Resolve optimization edge case mismatch in ax_position

This change fixes a DCHECK failure in AXPosition::CompareTo. It is a
pre-existing, Mac-only (kSuppressCharacter) disagreement between the
fast and slow comparison paths in ui/accessibility/ax_position.h,
triggered whenever an unignored, text-less leaf sits right after a
paragraph end. It also fixes the release-build case, where the same
comparisons quietly give inconsistent order. The extra cost is that
comparisons involving a paragraph-end position now take the slow path.

parent
c78ddb04a62433946ef3790e73da26da5f589b8d [ diff ] 
[Signin] Skip /ListAccounts when there are no Gaia cookies

GaiaCookieManagerService sends /ListAccounts whenever the cached list is
stale, which is always the case on a fresh profile. The first caller of
IdentityManager::GetAccountsInCookieJar() at startup therefore makes a
request to accounts.google.com even when the cookie jar has no Gaia
cookies, in which case the response is known to contain no accounts.

Before sending /ListAccounts, check the cookie jar for cookies on the
Gaia origin. If there are none, complete the request locally with an
empty account list. A Gaia cookie added later still triggers
/ListAccounts through the existing cookie change listener.

The behavior is behind kSkipListAccountsWithoutGaiaCookies, disabled by
default for a server-side rollout and enabled for tests in
fieldtrial_testing_config.json. Tests that fake Gaia either opt out of
the check (IdentityTestEnvironment and the identity_test_utils helpers,
which fake /ListAccounts responses) or set a SAPISID cookie like a real
web sign-in does (ActiveUserTestMixin, DiceBrowserTest,
DiceMigrationServiceBrowserTest and the sync device info test).

[Autofill AI] Use LegalMessage.token bytes as upsert context token

Replaces the top-level `GetDetailsForUpsertPassResponse.context_token`
string with `LegalMessage.token` (`bytes`) for Wallet public pass
upsert flows:

- Removes top-level `context_token` from
  `GetDetailsForUpsertPassResponse` and
  `WalletHttpClient::PassUpsertDetails`, extracting the token from
  `LegalMessage::token` in `WalletPassAccessManagerImpl` instead.
- Changes `AutofillValuableSpecifics.context_token` from `string` to
  `bytes` so binary tokens are serialized without UTF-8 validation.
- Base64-encodes and decodes `context_token` at the `autofillPrivate`
  extension API and Android JNI boundaries so arbitrary bytes
  round-trip safely through JS and Java strings.

Note that immediately after landing this change, I would need to
trigger capybara to update the sync code and sightly update the
generated code to make presubmit pass.

NO_IFTTT=context_token is already cleared in valuables_sync_util.cc

b377af402f0431c42d98ab41677cd983ad3c9163 [ diff ] 
Fetch: implement "create a proxy" in the Request constructor

The constructor still followed a version of the Fetch Standard that was
replaced in 2017. It made an empty dummyStream, gave that to the *input*
request as its body, and disturbed it. The input therefore ended up with
a new ReadableStream object, while the new request kept the original
one.

The standard does the opposite. The input keeps its own stream, which
becomes locked and disturbed, and the new request gets a separate stream
carrying the same data:

  Let finalBody be inputOrInitBody.
  If initBody is null and inputBody is non-null, then:
    If inputBody is unusable, then throw a TypeError.
    Set finalBody to the result of creating a proxy for inputBody.

Add BodyStreamBuffer::CreateProxy() for that. It builds on
ReleaseHandle(), which already behaves correctly for the common case: it
takes the underlying consumer, then closes, locks and disturbs this
buffer's stream, leaving the stream object itself in place. The old
dummy-stream swap also ran every time, where the standard runs this
branch only when init supplies no body. The new code matches.

A body backed by a JS ReadableStream takes the other path in
ReleaseHandle(), which returns a consumer that takes its own reader.
That locks the stream but does not disturb it until something reads.
Creating a proxy disturbs at once, so mark the stream disturbed there.
Without that, this change would regress bodyUsed for duplex requests,
which no web platform test covers. LockAndDisturb() cannot be used,
because it returns early once the stream is locked, hence the
implementation of ReadableStream::MarkDisturbed().

[TabModel] Replace getTabsInGroup().size() with getTabCountForGroup()

Calling getTabsInGroup(tabGroupId).size() crosses JNI to allocate and
marshal a C++ std::vector<TabAndroid*> into a Java List<Tab> solely to
query its length.

During tab restoration (TabCollectionTabModelImpl.addTabInternal),
restoring tabs in a group evaluated this check for every added tab,
causing repeated list allocations and object conversions.
NestedLayoutDelegate.removeChildTabs and TabGridDialogMediator similarly
only require the group size for layout and title updates.

Replace getTabsInGroup().size() with primitive getTabCountForGroup()
across these call sites to eliminate redundant container allocations.

[iOS][Actor] Add chat message interception skeleton

Adds an optional `handleChatMessageRequest:completion:` to
`GeminiSessionDelegate` so Chrome can consume Gemini Floaty chat
messages that answer ongoing actor tasks (e.g. clarification requests)
instead of sending them to Gemini. `GeminiSessionHandler` forwards to a
new `GeminiChatMessageHandler`, implemented by `GeminiActuationHandler`,
which never consumes messages for now. The completion must be called
synchronously, matching the Gemini SDK.

[Test] Deflake DefaultSearchEngineDialogTest on desktop

Switch BaseActivityTestRule from a per-test @Rule to a @ClassRule so
test cases in the batch share a single BlankUiTestActivity instance,
which avoids per-test activity launch races on desktop and makes the
suite run faster. To keep shared state clean between test cases, wait
for window focus in setUp and dismiss any remaining modal dialogs in
tearDown. Also verify the engine radio button is checked and the
confirm button is enabled before clicking confirm, and re-enable both
button click tests on desktop.

[css] Reject computationally dependent colors in OffscreenCanvas

OffscreenCanvas color assignments currently resolve font-relative
calculations using an empty length-conversion context, causing values
such as `em` to resolve as zero and unexpectedly replace the existing
fill or stroke color.

This change treats context-dependent calculations in OffscreenCanvas
color values as parse failures, matching new WPT expectations and
current Gecko/WebKit behavior. This is being tracked in
https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12505.

Since Blink's behavior is the outlier and is not intentional, adjusting
for interop makes the most sense.

[BottomSheetTypes] Migrate GroupSuggestionsBottomSheetContent to BottomSheetType

Migrates GroupSuggestionsBottomSheetContent from the legacy
ContentPriority system to the decomposed BottomSheetType architecture.

grouping heuristics rather than an explicit user action, this sheet is
configured as PASSIVE_PROMO (isUserInitiated = false, isModal = true,

Move permissions::PermissionRequestManager to TabFeatures

Migrate the attachment of permissions::PermissionRequestManager from
TabHelpers::AttachTabHelpers to Desktop and Android TabFeatures
(including TabFeatures::WillDiscardContents on Desktop).

Also attach PermissionRequestManager directly in
ChromeThinWebViewInitializer::AttachTabHelpers before configuring
set_web_contents_supports_permission_requests, since ThinWebView is a
non-tab surface that does not instantiate TabFeatures.

PermissionRequestManager lives in //components/permissions and is also
attached to non-tab WebContents in ChromeThinWebViewInitializer,
DocumentPipHost, PaymentHandlerWebFlowViewController,
ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator, OmniboxPopupWebuiBaseContent,
OmniboxEverywhereUiManager, VrUiHostImpl, and ExternalAppDialog, so
WebContents must continue to own it.

Flush pending text at the end of each chunk for HTMLStream

Flush pending text (including kTextMode) at the end of each chunk and before StopParsing() for fragment parsers, so written text is in the DOM when write() resolves and no text is left buffered in HTMLConstructionSite when a writer is dropped, aborted, or its write() rejects.

Handle displaced reference node and stop parsing on write error in HTMLStream

When the reference node (next_child) is removed or moved out of its
expected parent mid-chunk (e.g. by a streamed inline script), drop
subsequent nodes, text, and foster-parented children instead of hitting
a DCHECK in ContainerNode::ParserInsertBefore or appending to the old
parent.

Also call parser_->StopParsing() in HTMLSink::write before throwing on
chunk string conversion failure or a displaced reference node, matching
the spec's writeSteps abort behavior.

[EnterprisePolicy] Allow invalid list entries in AutofillSettings policy

Update AutofillSettingsPolicyHandler (and iOS BuildPolicyHandlerList) to
use SCHEMA_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_AND_INVALID_LIST_ENTRY instead of
SCHEMA_ALLOW_UNKNOWN.

Previously, an unknown category string in blocked_types or a malformed
list entry caused Schema::Validate() to fail during
CheckPolicySettings(), rejecting the entire AutofillSettings policy and
preventing valid co-existing rules from being applied to
prefs::kAutofillTypesBlocked. With
SCHEMA_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_AND_INVALID_LIST_ENTRY, schema validation logs a
non-fatal warning and still applies the policy so AutofillPolicyService
can enforce valid entries while ignoring malformed ones.

Disable features::kPrewarm in InProcessBrowserTest on win-asan

After crrev.com/c/8161122 configured a default production prewarm URL in
ChromeContentBrowserClient::GetPrewarmUrl(), every InProcessBrowserTest
spawns an extra prerender FrameTree and renderer process and warms up a
compositor for https://www.google.com/search/warmup.html during browser
startup (before failing with ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED because external DNS
resolution is disabled in InProcessBrowserTest).

On Windows under AddressSanitizer (win-asan), this extra process
creation and compositor warmup per test added ~436 minutes (+7.6%) of
total shard runtime to browser_tests, contributing to 60-minute shard
timeouts.

Disable features::kPrewarm by default in
InProcessBrowserTest::Initialize() when BUILDFLAG(IS_WIN) &&
defined(ADDRESS_SANITIZER), similar to how interactive_ui_tests disables
it in InteractiveUITestSuite::Initialize(). Dedicated prewarm browser
tests continue to test prewarming on win-asan because their
ScopedPrewarmFeatureList overrides InProcessBrowserTest's
scoped_feature_list_ in subclass constructors, and all other builders
keep default prewarm test coverage.

Move RequestDesktopSiteWebContentsObserverAndroid to TabFeatures

Migrate the attachment of RequestDesktopSiteWebContentsObserverAndroid
from TabHelpers::AttachTabHelpers to Android TabFeatures.

Also attach RequestDesktopSiteWebContentsObserverAndroid directly to
pre-tab WebContents on Android in
ChromeExtensionHostDelegate::CreateTab,
TabWebContentsDelegateAndroid::AddNewContents, and
PrerenderWebContentsDelegateImpl::PrerenderWebContentsCreated, where
navigation starts before TabAndroid (and TabFeatures) is created so
DidStartNavigation can override the user agent for the initial load.

Migrate the attachment of safe_browsing::SafeBrowsingNavigationObserver
from TabHelpers::AttachTabHelpers to Desktop and Android TabFeatures
(including TabFeatures::WillDiscardContents on Desktop).

SafeBrowsingNavigationObserver lives in

SafeBrowsingNavigationObserverManager, and cleans up in
WebContentsDestroyed() after TabFeatures is destroyed, so WebContents
must continue to own it.

[Actor] Record Actor.Notification.FetchTabId.Status on click

Records the Actor.Notification.FetchTabId.Status enum histogram when
a user clicks an Actor notification to bring the actuated tab to the
front:
- SUCCESS (0): Tab was found and selected synchronously or after tab
  state restoration.
- TAB_NOT_FOUND (1): TabModelSelector is null or already initialized
  without the target tab.
- TAB_CLOSED (2): Target tab is closing or destroyed.
- INVALID_ID (3): Notification intent had Tab.INVALID_TAB_ID.
- TIMEOUT (4): Tab state initialization completed without the target
  tab being added.

TAG=agy
CONV=e68a3116-cd24-403a-b860-0e040a2b1994

[a11y][1/2] Fix LabelButton text and icon visibility on hover in High Contrast

In forced-colors (high contrast) mode, UsingPlatformHighContrastInkDrop
sets the ink drop highlight opacity to 1.0f. In views::LabelButton,
ink_drop_container_ paints to a ui::Layer while label_ does not by
default, causing any opaque ink drop layer (or LayerRegion::kAbove ink
drop) to composite on top of label_ and hide the button text on hover
(affecting bookmarks bar buttons/folders, toolbar chips such as
ToolbarGlicButton and AvatarToolbarButton, etc.). Additionally, while
LabelButton::GetImage() updated the icon color to ui::kColorIconHovered
(COLOR_HIGHLIGHTTEXT) when highlighted by an opaque ink drop in
forced-colors mode, ResetLabelEnabledColor() did not update the label
text color, and neither fell back when the ink drop base color itself
matched ui::kColorIconHovered (such as TabCloseButton on an active or
hovered tab).

This CL:
- Paints LabelButton::label_ to a non-opaque layer (and disables
  subpixel rendering) when UsingPlatformHighContrastInkDrop is active,
  tracking whether LabelButton created the layer so subclass-owned
  layers are preserved when leaving high-contrast mode.
- Updates LabelButton::ResetLabelEnabledColor() and SetTextColor() to
  use ui::kColorIconHovered when UsingPlatformHighContrastInkDrop is
  active and an opaque ink drop highlight is visible.
- Falls back to color_utils::GetColorWithMaxContrast(base_color) in
  LabelButton::GetImage() and ResetLabelEnabledColor() when
  ui::kColorIconHovered has insufficient contrast against an opaque
  ink drop base color.

Demo: https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NDUxNjk3MDQ0NjcxNjkyOHxmZGI2Yzc5Yi0xNA

[TTC] Gate page context on actor safety lists

Before emitting extracted page context to observers,
TtcPageContextMonitor now asks actor::SafetyListManager whether a
navigation from the page URL to itself is allowed. If the safety
lists block it, the page is neither scraped nor surfaced.

This uses the same evaluation as the actor's safety list gating
predicate (CreateSafetyListPredicate() in
chrome/browser/actor/execution_engine.cc) for an event with no distinct
source: the destination is used as the source, and only
Decision::kBlock is treated as prohibited. The check fails open: if the
lists have not been loaded, nothing is blocked.

Caveat: navigation_blocked entries are (from, to) pairs. Because the
page URL is used as both source and destination, an entry like
{from: bank.com, to: *}, which is meant to stop the actor navigating
away from bank.com, also blocks reading bank.com. Entries like
{from: *, to: bank.com} block reading as intended. The actor's other
sensitive-site gate (MaybeCheckOptimizationGuideForSensitiveUrl() in
chrome/browser/actor/site_policy.h) is not applied here.

[PI] Rename AutofillClient::HideAmbientAutofillNotice().

The method used to hide the only notice the Touch To Fill autofill sheet
could show, the Personal Context ambient autofill notice, and was named
after it. Now that the sheet also shows the Autofill AI private
inference notice, it hides whichever of the two is up, which its comment
already says.

Renames it to HideTouchToFillAutofillNotice(), matching that comment and
the HideTouchToFill() method on TouchToFillAutofillDelegate that reaches
it. ShowAmbientAutofillNotice() keeps its name: unlike the hide method
it is specific to one notice, and "ambient autofill notice" is the term
Personal Context uses for it elsewhere.

This is a pure rename. The only production caller is
TouchToFillAutofillDelegateAndroidImpl.

[PI] Don't show the PI message when the TTF bottom sheet is enabled.

With kAutofillAiPrivateInferenceNoticeBottomSheet enabled, the Autofill
AI private inference notice is shown in the Touch To Fill bottom sheet.
BrowserAutofillManager::MaybeShowPrivateInferenceNotice() now returns
early on Android in that case, so that the Android message is not shown
in addition to the bottom sheet.

The method is still needed on iOS, which shows its own notice. A TODO
describes the cleanup once the flag has launched.

[Actor]: Register AttemptOtpFillingToolRequest in ToolRegistry

actor::ToolRegistry finds tool schemas by calling GetToolDefinition()
on each ToolRequest type in ToolRequestVariant. Each registered tool
declares its model-facing name, description and parameters with
ToolDefinitionBuilder.

AttemptOtpFillingToolRequest has no tool definition yet, so the
registry does not expose the OTP filling tool to the model.

This CL adds ToolId::kAttemptOtpFilling, the attempt_otp_filling
model-facing name, parameter key constants, and a GetToolDefinition()
with a trigger_field_dom_node_ids integer array and a for_signin
boolean. predicted_otp_type is not exposed since it is optional and
defaults to kUnknown. The tests check the schema and that the registry
discovers the tool.

Record Net.Android.BindToNetworkDuration histogram

Record a new custom-microseconds histogram,
Net.Android.BindToNetworkDuration, in net::android::BindToNetwork() to
measure the time spent in the android_setsocknetwork() NDK call. This
call is suspected to be slow as it performs a synchronous IPC to netd.

Save errno immediately after marshmallow_set_network_for_socket()
returns so that recording the histogram cannot overwrite errno on
failure.

[Skills] Restrict "Extensions and Skills" menu item to Glic-enabled users

Constrain the visibility of the "Extensions and Skills" entry in the
Chrome App Menu to profiles where Glic is enabled
(glic::GlicEnabling::IsEnabledForProfile), in addition to existing
skills feature and service checks.

When Glic is disabled or unavailable, the standard "Extensions" submenu
(or "Find extensions") remains visible.

Also update the visibility of kActionSkillsAndExtensionsSubmenu,
kActionExtensionsSubmenu, and kActionFindExtensions in
BrowserCommandController::UpdateCommandsForEnableGlicChanged() when Glic
enablement changes.

Accept Callback<? super T> in ObservableSupplier observer methods

Update add*Observer and removeObserver on NullableObservableSupplier,
MonotonicObservableSupplier, NonNullObservableSupplier, and
LookAheadObservableSupplier (along with their implementations) to take
contravariant Callback<? super T> instead of invariant Callback<T>.

This allows callers to register callbacks that capture base classes or
interfaces rather than requiring exact concrete types.

[GPU] Rename GpuInit1 to GpuInitLegacy

Rename GpuInit1 to GpuInitLegacy to make its role clearer: it is the
current, shipping initialization path, while GpuInit2 is the path where
GPU startup optimizations are being developed (behind
features::kGpuInitOptimization).

Also unify the TRACE_EVENT names in both implementations to
"gpu::GpuInit::*" so traces are comparable regardless of which path is
taken, and update related comments.

No functional change.

[iOS] Prevent rewriting non-app-specific URLs to app-specific on restore

Prevent NavigationManagerImpl::RewriteItemURLIfNecessary() from
rewriting a persisted non-app-specific URL into an app-specific URL
during session restoration, matching the check in
CreateNavigationItemWithRewriters().

Also tighten WillHandleWebBrowserAboutURL() to only process about: and

chrome: URLs before calling url_formatter::FixupURL(), and prevent
HandleViewSource() from unwrapping view-source: when the inner URL is
an app-specific URL.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in base/process/launch

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

parent
4c42a0dba978b9c8af5106e42438d5010801b3ea [ diff ] 
Set WebSocketCommon state to kClosed when WebSocketStream aborts

When WebSocketStream::OnAbort() cancelled the handshake and reset
channel_ to nullptr, it left common_ in the kConnecting state. Calling
close() afterwards passed a null channel_ to
WebSocketCommon::CloseInternal() while in kConnecting, causing a null
pointer dereference in WebSocketChannelImpl::Fail().

Similarly, when WebSocketStream::Connect() returned early due to an
already-aborted signal, common_ remained in kConnecting and channel_ was
not cleared, keeping HasPendingActivity() true and causing subsequent
close() calls to fail an unconnected channel.

Set common_ to kClosed and clear channel_ in both abort paths, and clear
channel_ and abort_handle_ when Connect() fails asynchronously.

[FragmentedOofInCb] Relayout self-collapsed on BFC block-offset change.

Inside block fragmentation, if there are any OOFs inside a
self-collapsing block whose initial BFC block-offset estimate was wrong,
we need to relayout, just like we already do for adjoining floats. This
is not an issue for non-FragmentedOofInCb, since then all OOF layout is
delayed until right before finishing layout of the outermost
fragmentation context root.

The two tests included would fail when run as
virtual/fragmented-oof-in-cb/.

Clear failed favicon downloads when clearing browsing data

FaviconService maintains an in-memory set of favicon URLs that failed to
download. Leaving this negative cache intact after clearing data can
leak browsing history or potentially be used to re-identify users.

This change ensures that the failed favicon download cache is cleared
whenever browsing history or cache data is removed.

parent
5750cc1f2e15205a18a802254598052c3d02de35 [ diff ] 
Fix ui GetApplicationLocale fallback matching algorithm

When we have the LANGUAGE env var set with multiple locale options, we
would prioritize exact matches. The bug report clearly shows that
this should not be the case and we should return the first match we get.
For example:

- "de_DE:en_US": we should return "de" rather than "en_US" even though there is an exact match on-disk for "en_US" but "de" is much closer to "de_DE" which is the first preferred locale.

This fix is assuming that it is always preferred to match the first
candidates rather than picking an exact match that comes later in the
preferred locales list.

[Autofill AI] Log Wallet notice settings funnel on iOS

Extends `Autofill.Ai.WalletNotice.Settings.Funnel` to iOS settings when
adding a public pass in `AutofillAIEntityEditTableViewController` and
`AutofillAIEntityEditMediator`. Preload fetch events
(`kFetchingUpsertDetails`, `kUpsertDetailsFetchSuccess`, and
`kUpsertDetailsFetchError`) are already recorded in
`WalletPassAccessManagerImpl`.

Specifically:
- Logs `kLegalMessageShown` (`/*in_settings=*/true`) in
  `AutofillAIEntityEditTableViewController` when non-empty legal
  messages are set.
- Tracks `_legalMessageURLs` separately from the storage notice URL in
  `AutofillAIEntityEditTableViewController` and logs `kLinkClicked`
  (`/*in_settings=*/true`) when a legal message link is tapped.
- Logs `kEntitySaved` (`/*in_settings=*/true`) in
  `AutofillAIEntityEditMediator::saveEntityInstance` when saving an
  entity with a disclosure `_contextToken`.
- Adds `disconnect` to `AutofillAIEntityEditMediator` (invoked from
  `AutofillAIEntityEditCoordinator::stop`, including on modal swipe
  dismissal) to log `kEntityNotSaved` (`/*in_settings=*/true`) if
  `_contextToken` was never consumed by a save.
- Updates the `Settings` variant summary in `histograms.xml` to be
  platform-neutral.

[ios] Fix fullscreen progress desync when omnibox is at the bottom

When the omnibox is at the bottom, the top collapsible inset range is
zero (top_delta == 0). IncrementalScroll previously only updated
top_progress_ using top_delta, leaving top_progress_ stuck at 1.0 even
as bottom_progress_ collapsed to 0.0. When dragging stopped or when
transitions triggered, logic checking top_progress_ or State() falsely
treated the UI as expanded, triggering conflicting exit transitions
and causing jerky snaps.

Additionally, IncrementalScroll only guarded against in-flight
animations when FullscreenEasedTransitions was enabled, allowing
residual scroll events during deceleration to interrupt animations.

This CL:
- Synchronizes top_progress_ with bottom_progress_ when only the bottom
  edge has collapsible insets (and vice versa).
- Unconditionally ignores IncrementalScroll while is_animating_ is
  active.
- Adds a unit test covering bottom-only collapsible insets and scroll
  interruption protection.

Reland "[omnibox] Add bubble window-switch test and one-shot check helpers"

This is a reland of commit 8f496fcfc46b74ad8bfe5f23411ae91cade4bd43

The original change was reverted because
WindowSwitchWhileBubbleActiveDismissesPopup failed on
linux-wayland-mutter-rel-tests (and linux-arm64-wayland-rel-fyi). On
Wayland, activating the test bubble already blurs the omnibox, so the
test's precondition doesn't hold. This reland skips that test on
Wayland. b:571715601 tracks re-enabling it there.

Original change's description:
> [omnibox] Add bubble window-switch test and one-shot check helpers
>
> * Adds WindowSwitchWhileBubbleActiveDismissesPopup. It switches windows
> while a bubble is active, so neither the browser nor the popup widget
> gets an activation change and only the paint-as-active subscription can
> blur the omnibox.
> * Adds one-shot versions of the polling focus and popup-state helpers, to make focus validation tighter.
> * Make tests start on NTPs, so we have more test coverage. Currently, these tests start with `about:blank`. Starting with the NTP is the default case for a browser where a user didn't change their startup page. And this gives us more coverage for the "Views Omnibox to WebUI Omnibox handoff" story.

optimization_guide: remove unused //ui/accessibility dep from :features

//components/optimization_guide/core:features does not include any
headers from //ui/accessibility, but had it in public_deps. Because
//ui/accessibility depends on //ui/accessibility/platform -> //gin ->
//v8, this unnecessary public_dep forced
libcomponents_optimization_guide_core_features.so (and downstream
targets like //components/language_detection/core and
//third_party/blink/public/common) to wait for libv8.so to finish
linking on the critical path.

Removing this unused public_dep removes 5 serial link steps between
libv8.so and libblink_platform.so on the clean build critical path. Also
add direct //ui/base dependencies to two targets that were transitively
relying on it through //ui/accessibility.

compile_resources.py: Avoid android.jar in ExtractBinaryManifestValues

ExtractBinaryManifestValues() runs `aapt2 dump xmltree` on android.jar
to extract platformBuildVersionCode and platformBuildVersionName from
its binary AndroidManifest.xml. Because android.jar also contains a 22
MB resources.arsc table, aapt2 spent ~0.72s loading and parsing
resources.arsc before dumping the 4 KB AndroidManifest.xml.

Extracting just AndroidManifest.xml into a temporary zip before calling
`aapt2 dump xmltree` reduces ExtractBinaryManifestValues() from ~0.72s
to ~0.06s.

SessionServiceImpl is growing too large, and all DBSC-SSO key operations
will live in SingleSignOnKeyManager (IdP key creation, GenerateKey, and
AIK restore will follow in upcoming CLs).

Move pre-provisioned key storage, insertion, lookup, consumption, and
clearing from SessionServiceImpl into SingleSignOnKeyManager. Remove
AddPreProvisionedKey and FindPreProvisionedKey from the SessionService
interface, as only SessionServiceImpl and its tests need them.

No behavior change.

Avoid holding Attribute& across WillModifyAttribute()

WillModifyAttribute() invokes probe::WillModifyDOMAttr(), which can
synchronously pause in the DevTools debugger when an attribute-modified
DOM breakpoint is set on the element. While paused, the debugger client
can evaluate script that mutates the element's attributes and
reallocates the attribute vector backing.

Look up EnsureUniqueElementData().Attributes() after
WillModifyAttribute() in SetAttributeInternal() and
RemoveAttributeInternal() instead of holding a raw Attribute& or
MutableAttributeCollection across the call.

compile_resources.py: Check package ID via R.txt instead of aapt2

compile_resources.py previously called ExtractArscPackage(), which
spawned `aapt2 dump resources` on the output .ap_ to verify the linked
package ID. For chrome_public_apk, `aapt2 dump resources` took ~0.79s to
parse the 38 MB resources.arsc table before printing the Package header
line.

Since `aapt2 link` already writes `build.r_txt_path` via
`--output-text-symbols`, read the package ID from the first
non-styleable `int` entry in R.txt (<0.1ms) and remove the unused
ExtractArscPackage() helper.

[Masonry] Fragment nested dense-packed items

Fragmented grid-lanes iteration previously walked only each lane's root
item vector. Items stored above another item by dense packing were
skipped, and spanners whose entries had different nested paths in each
lane could not be resumed consistently.

Use lane-local item index paths to walk nested storage in physical
stacking order. Normal columns and rows visit dense children before
their parent, while fill-reverse columns visit the recursively reversed
parent first.

Update UOOM ineligibility state even if the toggle is enabled

Previously, a user remained marked as eligible for universal opt-out if
they had the toggle enabled. This changes the eligibility check so that
a user becomes ineligible purely based on the eligibility category,
regardless of whether the opt-out toggle is enabled.

UI clients still check the value of both the toggle and eligibility to
determine whether to show the setting.

Android: Skip aapt2 convert when --proto-path is not specified

compile_resources.py previously ran `aapt2 convert --output-format
proto` unconditionally even when `--proto-path` was not passed (a
leftover from when `--shared-resources` was removed in
https://crrev.com/c/6799242). For non-bundle APK targets like
`chrome_public_apk__compile_resources`, this spent ~4.0s converting the
41 MB .ap_ into a temporary .proto.ap_ that was immediately discarded.

Skipping `aapt2 convert` when `options.proto_path` is None reduces
`chrome_public_apk__compile_resources` wall time by ~4.0s (-35%).

[Actor]: Add AddArrayProperty to ToolSchemaBuilder

Actor tools describe their parameters to the model with
ToolSchemaBuilder, which builds a JSON Schema object for each tool in
actor::ToolRegistry.

ToolSchemaBuilder supports string, enum, integer, number and boolean
properties, but not arrays. The attempt_otp_filling tool takes a list
of DOM node IDs, and file_upload and load_and_extract_content take
lists of strings.

This CL adds ToolSchemaBuilder::AddArrayProperty(), which adds a
required array property whose items have a given scalar type, plus
unit tests for integer and string items.

android_webview: Remove WebViewRendererKeepAlive feature

Remove the WebViewRendererKeepAlive feature and its
webview_renderer_keep_alive_duration param. The feature is enabled by
default, so this makes the current behavior unconditional: a renderer
is always kept alive after its last WebView is destroyed, so that the
next WebView can reuse it.

Also remove the keep-alive timer from AwRenderProcessKeepAlive. Its
default duration was 1000 days, so renderers were effectively already
kept alive forever. AddAwContents() now treats a renderer that is kept
alive but hosts no AwContents as pending reuse, which matches when the
timer used to be running. Delete the test for the timer duration.

The "Timed out" bucket of Android.WebView.RendererKeepAlive.Event can
no longer be recorded, so mark it as obsolete.

Don't throttle favicon display after navigation

BrowserUiController created perceived latency by waiting up to 200 ms
(kUIUpdateCoalescingTime) to show the favicon after cached navigations.

Set a new invalidation bit (INVALIDATE_TYPE_ICON) for the first display
of a valid favicon after a cross-document navigation finishes. Consume
in BrowserUiController to update the UI immediately instead of waiting.

If a page updates its favicon dynamically, those updates are still
throttled as before. The behavior of the throbber (synchronous update
for INVALIDATE_TYPE_LOAD) is also unaffected.

This change is guarded by a kill switch (FastFaviconDisplay), so it can
be disabled in the event of a regression.

[iOS] Verify actual URL before allowing app-specific navigations

A committed NavigationItem can have its virtual URL overridden to an
app-specific `chrome://` URL for UI display while its actual loaded URL
is not app-specific (for example, `about://newtab/` has its virtual URL
set to `chrome://newtab/`). Previously, `-[CRWWKNavigationHandler
shouldAllowAppSpecificURLNavigationAction:transition:]` only checked
whether the last committed item's `GetVirtualURL()` was app-specific,
which allowed a non-app-specific page with an app-specific virtual URL
to perform renderer-initiated navigations to arbitrary `chrome://`
WebUI URLs.

Require both `GetVirtualURL()` and `GetURL()` of the last committed
NavigationItem to be app-specific before granting privileges to
navigate to other app-specific URLs.

[XDeviceSignin] Prevent premature dismissal of cross-device signin promo

Previously, the history cross-device sign-in promo would disappear
unconditionally when the user closed the QR code bubble, even if they
did not complete the sign-in process. This happened because the UI was
hardcoded to hide the promo as soon as the action click promise
resolved.

Keep the promo card visible when the QR code bubble closes (or when no
bubble was opened), re-enabling the CTA button so the user can reopen
the bubble. Hiding the card once the user is no longer eligible is
handled in a follow-up CL.

parent
f92660c3a424d3803dd2e3f91804438d1fb03e88 [ diff ] 
audio: Report InputController errors to EventHandler at most once

InputController reported errors through two paths: three direct
EventHandler::OnError() calls in DoCreate(), and DoReportError() for
everything else. Nothing prevented a second error from reaching the
EventHandler. In particular, VoiceIsolationHandler initializes its
component asynchronously on the ThreadPool and reports a failure via
DoReportError(STREAM_ERROR); if DoCreate() had already failed
(MakeAudioInputStream() returned null or Open() failed), the
EventHandler had already received STREAM_CREATE_ERROR / STREAM_OPEN_*
and could then receive a redundant STREAM_ERROR before InputStream's
posted teardown task ran.

Funnel all error reporting through DoReportError() and guard it with a
`can_report_error_` flag:
1. DoCreate() failure paths call DoReportError().
2. DoReportError() dispatches the first error and clears the flag.
3. Close() clears the flag.
Any later error is logged and dropped. A failed voice isolation
startup is still fully processed when the reply arrives: the broken
model is invalidated and startup metrics are recorded. (InputStream
deletes the controller on a posted task after the create error, so the
reply may instead be dropped via the handler's WeakPtr; metrics then
record kAborted.)

[iOS] Request continued processing tasks from providers on backgrounding

Adds a task provider registry to BackgroundContinuedProcessingAppAgent.
When the app enters the background, the agent notifies providers, asks
them for task requests, submits the requests and hands the context of
each started task back to its provider. Providers are also notified
when the app enters the foreground.

Requesting a task no longer requires a foreground scene, since requests
are now submitted once the app has entered the background.

No provider is registered yet; the actor registers one in a follow-up.

[iOS] Fix background snapshot hang in ToolbarViewController

The hang is caused by ToolbarViewController registering for
UITraitUserInterfaceStyle and invoking `-updateBackgroundColors` during
background scene-update snapshotting, where app CPU is heavily
throttled. Setting _locationBarBackground.backgroundColor on each
light/dark snapshot creates a dynamic color instance that cannot
short-circuit, triggering asset catalog lookups.

crrev.com/c/8324947 originally introduced this trait observation to
coordinate the scrolled-up toolbar background with the pinned omnibox
depending on the enabled status of `kNewTabPageUICleanup`.

This change:
1. Wraps the manual userInterfaceStyle check in
-toolbarBackgroundColor
   in `[UIColor colorWithDynamicProvider:]`, allowing UIKit to resolve
   light and dark colors natively on the view layer.
2. Removes the UITraitUserInterfaceStyle registration and
   -userInterfaceStyleDidChange from ToolbarViewController, avoiding
   redundant color recalculations during background snapshotting.
3. Preserves -updateBackgroundColors for NTP navigation, size class
   updates, and custom NTP theme/background trait changes.

Screen Recordings: Light Mode:
http://screencast/cast/NTU5ODU2MzcwNTgxNTA0MHw1ZjE4MWU2OS05OA Dark Mode:
http://screencast/cast/NTcxNjMxMTM3NTA4NTU2OHwyNDcxMDMzNS01NA

[webauthn] Add a fake CMTG server

Teach FakeCmtgDeviceKeyProvider to answer CryptAuth getOrCreate and
batchGet network requests, similar to FakeRecoveryKeyStore. This lets
browser tests exercise the real CryptauthCmtgDeviceKeyProvider against a
fake server, and is now the default for EnclaveAuthenticatorTestBase.

The fake now models the service instead of replaying canned keys. It
tracks a set of devices, each in a trust group, and answers as the
current device. Each device's key is created, with its creation time,
the first time the device fetches keys. getOrCreate returns the current
device's key, and batchGet returns it followed by the keys of the other
devices in its trust group. Tests can add devices, merge trust groups
and switch the current device. SetNextKeys and SetNextError remain to
simulate a misbehaving server.

Tests that need CMTG keys for assertions still use the fake provider
directly until the batchGet client lands.

[XDeviceSignin] Disable history promo CTA while the QR bubble is open

Because the "Sign in to phone" QR code bubble intentionally stays open
when interacting with web contents (close-on-deactivate is disabled),
users can view or navigate to chrome://history while the bubble is
already active. Previously, the History promo card had no visibility
into the bubble's state, leaving its CTA button enabled where clicking
it would destroy and recreate the existing bubble (recording duplicate
metrics) or open a second bubble in another window.

This CL tracks the QR bubble's open state per profile via Profile user
data (IsCrossDeviceSigninPromoBubbleOpen and
RegisterCrossDeviceSigninPromoBubbleStateCallback).
OpenSigninToPhoneQrCodeBubble() refuses to open a second bubble from
promo entry points while closing and reopening the bubble when triggered
from permanent entry points such as the profile menu or SendTabToSelf,
and the History WebUI promo card observes this state via Mojo to disable
its CTA button while the bubble is shown.

The History handler now also reports a bad Mojo message for action
clicks received while kCrossDeviceSigninFromDesktop is disabled. The
promo card is never shown then, so only a misbehaving renderer could
send one, and it used to reach the feature CHECK in
OpenSigninToPhoneQrCodeBubble().

Android: Implement single-pass zero-copy v2/v3 + v4 signing in ZipBuilder

Instead of running DefaultApkSignerEngine (which reads the APK twice via
ChunkSupplier and VerityTreeBuilder, allocating 2x APK_SIZE of heap byte
arrays via DataSource.copyTo), fuse v2/v3 1 MiB chunk hashing and v4 4
KiB fs-verity leaf hashing over direct MappedByteBuffer slices of the
ZIP payload in a single parallel pass. Once the v2/v3 APK Signing Block
is generated, finish the remaining ~320 KiB tail and upper verity tree
levels and invoke V4SchemeSigner.generateSignature.

Produces bit-for-bit identical .apk and .apk.idsig outputs while
reducing ChromePublic.apk (710 MB) end-to-end zip+sign time from ~1.07s
to ~0.89s.

Also adds graalvm image, which brings time to 0.583s

[iOS] Wait for the posted stop notification in a backgrounding test

Since ActorTask posts observer registrations and notifications
(crrev.com/c/8503447), BackgroundTaskStoppedWithShutdown asserts the
stop notification before it is delivered. The test only runs where actor
backgrounding is available (iOS 26 with background continued processing
enabled), which the CQ does not cover, so it only fails on builds with
the backgrounding flag enabled.

[iOS][DeviceAuth] Use device authorization keys for passkey assertion

This CL adds support for decrypting passkeys with device auth keys in
PasskeyTabHelper. The device auth key fetch is added right before the
trusted vault key fetch, as the former can fetch the latter in case it
displays the reauth UI, preventing the UI to be displayed twice.

API changes:
* added FetchDeviceAuthorizationKeys() in ios_passkey_client.h,
* modified flow in PasskeyTabHelper to fetch device auth keys for
passkeys with `security_domain_encrypted` encryption scheme, when the
feature is enabled

fuzzilli: Distinguish associated and non-associated interface types

Associated and non-associated endpoints of the same interface shared a
single Fuzzilli type, so Fuzzilli could pass e.g. the result of
`bindNewPipeAndPassReceiver` where a `pending_associated_receiver` was
expected.

Endpoints that JS passes as arguments now get one type per Mojom kind:
`PendingReceiver`, `PendingAssociatedReceiver`, `PendingRemote` and
`PendingAssociatedRemote`. Each is only emitted and registered when the
interface uses that kind. Remotes that JS calls into keep the `Remote`
type, which carries the interface's methods.

Revert "[iOS] Set ButtonStack scroll view identifier and fix file picker cancel"

This reverts commit 18a4effdf5fb2787af93a14c1e46be7e9609c1d3.

Reason for revert: Step "check_static_initializers" is failing on builder "chromium/ci/ios-device"

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/b/8668410497948965985

Original change's description:
> [iOS] Set ButtonStack scroll view identifier and fix file picker cancel
>
> When PromoStyleViewController was refactored to inherit from
> ButtonStackViewController, the assignment of
> kPromoStyleScrollViewAccessibilityIdentifier to the scroll view was
> lost as scroll view initialization moved to the base class. Set
> kButtonStackScrollViewAccessibilityIdentifier on the scroll view in
> ButtonStackViewController directly, and alias
> kPromoStyleScrollViewAccessibilityIdentifier to it. This fixes
> FirstRunWithUpdatedFRESequenceTestCase on devices where EarlGrey scrolls
> the promo view without exposing the scroll view property.
>
> In FileUploadPanelTestCase.testFilePickerCancel, the test previously
> attempted to double-tap the Browse button unconditionally on iPhone
> idioms to reveal the Cancel button, waiting for the Browse button to
> become selected. On iPhone Duo and iPad the Cancel button is already
> accessible directly in the navigation bar, and the Browse selection check
> timed out. Guard the Browse navigation behind checking if the Cancel
> button is already present, and use kShortWaitForCancelButtonTimeout with
> an explanatory comment.
>

parent
9a1b54011bac2948c61013ffe6b652873dcdb285 [ diff ] 
[glic] Record the client load state at invocation start

Invocations that fail with kClientLoadError in kWaitForClientReady with
no InvokeWebUiStateReached and no ClientLoadError event of their own are
the largest FAILED bucket on Canary. Nothing recorded today separates
the two ways that can happen: the invocation terminated synchronously
on a failure left over from an earlier show of the panel (the case
fixed in the parent change), or it watched a fresh failure that reached
the host before the page's state and reason messages (e.g. via
Host::WebClientInitializeFailed()).

Add ClientLoadStateAtStart to InvokeTerminated, carrying the targeted
host's ClientLoadState as observed before any of the invocation's tasks
run. LOAD_ERROR at start identifies the inherited-failure case, LOADING
the fresh one, and READY an invocation that lost a working client
midway. The field is absent for invocations rejected before they start,
which have no host to observe.

5eb5011e7fa32495fef90ae380a041a8874fd900 [ diff ] 
Android: Optimize ZipBuilder stored file CRC, scheduling, and mmap signing

 * Adds StoredFileSource for uncompressed loose files >= 64 KiB,
   computing CRC32 via FileChannel + a 256 KiB thread-local
   DirectByteBuffer and writing via FileChannel.transferTo (sendfile).
   Avoids zipflinger BytesSource's heap allocations (up to 100 MB) and
   LargeFileSource's 4 KiB CheckedInputStream loop (~295 ms -> ~111 ms
   on libchrome.so).
 * Moves ZipMap parsing and ZipSource entry selection off the main
   thread onto the worker pool, schedules the first entry followed by
   stored loose files in reverse order (putting libchrome.so on a worker
   thread immediately), and initializes the keystore/signer engine on
   the pool when v1 signing is disabled.
 * Bypasses SignedApk's FileChannelDataSource (which serializes all
   digest worker threads on synchronized(mChannel) and copies through
   temporary DirectByteBuffers) when v1 signing is disabled, mapping the
   output APK with MappedByteBuffer (ByteBufferDataSource) for v2/v3 and
   v4 signing.

Reduces ChromePublic.apk (745 MB) apkbuilder time from ~1.40s to ~1.08s
with bit-for-bit identical .apk and .apk.idsig outputs.

[iOS] Reload entity edit footer when its inputs change

`AutofillAIEntityEditTableViewController` built its footer only in
`loadModel`, while `setIsServerWalletItem:`, `setUserEmail:` and
`setLegalMessages:` merely stored their values. The mediator sets these
after the view has already loaded, so the Wallet storage notice and
legal disclosures were correct only because `setEditItems:` happened to
be called last and rebuild the whole model.

Make each footer input refresh the footer section itself. The refresh is
skipped once the view is on screen, preserving the guarantee that legal
disclosures never appear mid-session.

Tests are being moved out of chrome/test/BUILD.gn into per-directory
test targets. Add a presubmit check that warns when a CL adds a test
source (*test.cc or *test.mm) that lives outside //chrome/test to
chrome/test/BUILD.gn, pointing the author at a per-directory test
target instead.

("//chrome/common/bar/bar_browsertest.cc") paths are both handled.

between the old and new BUILD.gn, so moving an existing file within
the BUILD.gn or switching between relative and absolute paths does not
warn.

[iOS] Skip redundant scroll view contentSize and frame notifications

WKWebView sets `scrollView.contentSize` on every remote layer tree
commit (`_updateScrollViewForTransaction:`), even when `contentSize` has
not changed. Because Objective-C KVO fires on every setter invocation,
`CRWWebViewScrollViewProxy` was forwarding every call through
`CRBProtocolObservers` (`NSInvocation`) and `MainContentUIStateUpdater`
was re-setting `MainContentUIState.contentSize`, triggering a second KVO
round into `ChromeBroadcaster` before finally bailing out on unchanged
values.

This change:
1. Restores the KVO `oldValue`/`newValue` equality check in
   `-[CRWWebViewScrollViewProxy observeValueForKeyPath:ofObject:change:context:]`
   (which already registers with `NSKeyValueObservingOptionNew |
   NSKeyValueObservingOptionOld`).
2. Guards `scrollViewSizeDidChange:` and `scrollViewDidResetContentSize:`
   in `MainContentUIStateUpdater` when the size is unchanged.

[iOS] Add opt-in progress heartbeat to continued processing tasks

Adds a progressHeartbeatInterval configuration option. When set, the
task context advances progress by one unit per interval, up to
totalUnits - 1, so that slow but alive work keeps reporting progress.

Stepped progress now resumes at the next linear step boundary above the
current progress, so heartbeat units never cause a step to be skipped.

Dismiss the Glic selection prompt when a context menu opens

When a context menu is created, dismiss any active Glic selection UI and
clear any pending selection state so the widget does not appear after
drag-selection completes. Additionally, prevent the selection widget
from showing while the WebContents is displaying a context menu.

BUG=546644969
